title: Release-blocker fixes: regenerate Petopia logo (remove “Premium”) and standardize reliable image loading via TypeScript imports

requirements.text: Generate a brand-new Petopia logo system (wordmark + subtle pet icon) and replace ALL existing logo usages so the only displayed brand text is exactly “Petopia” (no “Premium” anywhere), with a single source of truth used across: navbar, footer, login/signup, cart/checkout/payment, confirmation pages, and any fallback/alt logo rendering.

quotes: The word “Premium” must be COMPLETELY removed from the logo.
GENERATE a brand-new logo for the company.
Use a wordmark + subtle icon combination.
There should be a single source of truth for the logo across the entire application.

acceptanceCriteria: Searching the codebase for the string "Premium" returns zero instances in logo/brand contexts (including SVG text, image names, alt/fallback content).
All pages that render a logo (global header/footer, /account/login, /account/signup, /cart, /checkout, /payment, and all confirmation pages) display the exact wordmark text “Petopia”.

There is exactly one reusable frontend component/module responsible for rendering the logo (icon + wordmark) and all other logo renderings delegate to it (no duplicate inline SVGs or hardcoded logo paths).

requirements.text: Update favicon to a simplified version derived directly from the new Petopia logo icon (not a letter), and ensure the HTML entry point references the updated favicon asset.

quotes: Use a simplified version of the logo icon (not a generic letter).

acceptanceCriteria: The favicon is visually recognizable at small sizes and matches the logo icon style.
frontend/index.html references the new favicon file and the favicon loads correctly in the browser tab on first load.

requirements.text: Standardize the entire in-app image strategy to TypeScript-imported assets (no mixed public-path images for in-app rendering): refactor content modules (e.g., products, adoption, blog, services) and page/components to use imported image references so images resolve reliably on all routes, including dynamic routes.

quotes: Standardize the entire project on ONE approach: Use imported image assets via TypeScript imports.
Images are currently not loading reliably.

acceptanceCriteria: In-app images (cards, heroes, galleries, thumbnails, order/cart summary images) are rendered from TypeScript imports rather than string paths like "/assets/...".
Navigation across dynamic routes (e.g., product detail, adoption species/breed/pet profile, blog topic/article) shows correct images on first load and on refresh (no broken images).
No components/pages reference broken absolute paths for in-app images (e.g., hardcoded "/assets/generated/..." in JSX for non-favicon use cases).

requirements.text: Improve image loading reliability across all pages by adding consistent loading behavior and fallbacks for lazy-loaded images (e.g., graceful placeholder/empty-state rendering when an image fails to load) so every card and detail page shows an image correctly on first load.

quotes:
Adding proper fallbacks for lazy-loaded images

Every card and detail page MUST show its image correctly on first load.

acceptanceCriteria: If an image fails to load, the UI displays a consistent fallback presentation instead of a broken-image icon or layout collapse.
Key listing/detail surfaces (Products, Services, Adoption, Blog) do not show missing/broken images during normal navigation and refresh scenarios.
Lazy-loaded images use consistent settings and do not cause blank gaps during initial render (especially in grids and galleries).

requirements.text: Run a release-blocking QA sweep and fix any remaining issues before marking the build complete: verify “Premium” is removed everywhere, verify zero broken images across the sitemap, and verify Adoption/Product/Service/Blog images load correctly on all routes.

quotes:
Do not proceed to hosting or mark the build complete until:
- “Premium” is removed everywhere
- No image is broken across any page
- Adoption, Product, Service, and Blog images load correctly on all routes

acceptanceCriteria: Manual QA pass confirms the three blocker conditions (no “Premium”, no broken images, correct image loading across Adoption/Product/Service/Blog) are satisfied across routed navigation and direct URL entry (refresh).
Any discovered broken routes or broken assets are fixed as part of this task, with no regressions in cart/checkout/payment navigation.

constraints: Frontend-only scope for this blocker pass; do not add or change backend features/APIs.
Do not edit files under frontend/src/components/ui or the immutable hook/entry files listed in SYSTEM_CONTEXT.
Standardize in-app images on TypeScript imports (no mixed public-path strategy for in-app rendering).
Favicon must remain referenced from frontend/index.html (static file reference is required by HTML).
nonGoals: Regenerating or replacing all images site-wide; only replace images that are broken, mismatched with content, or overly generic where specificity is required.
Adding new pages or changing sitemap/IA beyond what is necessary to fix logo and image-loading blockers.
Rebuilding checkout/payment UX or auth UX beyond what is necessary to fix logo/image issues.

required: Petopia wordmark + icon horizontal lockup on light background (petopia-logo-lockup.dim_1400x400.png)
Petopia favicon derived from the logo icon (petopia-favicon.dim_64x64.png)
